clue.text: Iris, artist with popular archer

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a bow can mean an archer, as in a company of bows

explanation.surface: A painter keeps company with a well-liked bowman called Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris looks like a woman's name; she was the Greek goddess of the rainbow, and iris is also an old word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is the classical personification of the coloured arc in the sky, and the word itself once named it.

clue.text: Replace striker in second game between teams

blocks.note: to replace something is to put it back, return it
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A football manager swaps the centre forward for a team's rematch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer but is something you strike on a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A follow-up fixture played after an earlier meeting between the same two sides gets this name.

clue.text: Girl holding key for Welshman

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so the girl's name goes round

explanation.surface: A girl has the key that belongs to a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: IRIS with D inside gives IDRIS, a Welsh name borne by a giant of Welsh legend.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional male Christian name from Wales, so a person bearing it stands for a man of that nation.

clue.text: Have in cheese and cake

indicators.note: in places the verb's synonym inside the cheese word

explanation.surface: An invitation to eat cheese and a piece of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' looks like an invitation to eat, but it is a synonym meaning possess.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense, fudgy chocolate square served as a small baked treat is this sort of cake.

clue.text: Time to bring down the curtain, taking everything into consideration?

annotation.answer: WHEN ALL IS SAID AND DONE

definitions.text: Time to bring down the curtain

blocks.clueFragment: Time to bring down the curtain
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: the moment once every line is spoken and every act performed
second meaning: the idiom for 'in the final analysis'

explanation.surface: A stage manager judges the right moment to end the show, all things considered.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the idiom literally: once all is said and done, the play is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'ultimately, on balance', and literally names the point when talk and action are finished.

clue.text: After opening of boutique, all, note, have formal dress

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the shop word

explanation.surface: Once the boutique opens, every woman wants an evening gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, elegant gown worn to a dance or formal evening party is the formal dress meant.

clue.text: Sweetheart gets upset about ending in feature film

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and land in a new order
the ending in a word is its last letter alone
about means going around, so the shuffled letters sit either side of the single letter

explanation.surface: A girlfriend gets annoyed about how a feature film ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature film' looks like one phrase, but 'film' alone is the definition. Beau Geste is P C Wren's Foreign Legion story, filmed several times.
explanation.definitionFit: The adventure novel was made into several famous Hollywood pictures, notably the 1939 version with Gary Cooper.

clue.text: Shows the way in speech in Yorkshire city

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard rather than seen spelt

blocks.note: a guide who shows the way leads

explanation.surface: Someone guides people through a city in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large city in West Yorkshire, the county in northern England.

clue.text: Jazzman‘s guide covering EP with singular content

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one word goes outside the other
with a letter as its content means that letter goes inside
a content sits inside something, so this letter is placed within

blocks.note: a gillie is a Scottish hunting or fishing guide
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A jazz guide describes a record whose contents are unique.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie is a Scottish gamekeeper's attendant; 'guide' looks like a book. Dizzy Gillespie was the bebop trumpeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy Gillespie was a celebrated American trumpeter and bandleader, one of the founders of bebop.

clue.text: Punishment? Why?

blocks.note: first meaning: a telling-off, as in 'give someone ...'
second meaning: a casual way of asking for a reason

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate questions in the surface, but each is one meaning of the same informal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone this means scolding or punishing them, and the phrase also asks for a purpose, like 'for what reason?'

clue.text: Strange assignment for henchman in film

explanation.surface: A villain's sidekick is given a peculiar task.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddjob is Goldfinger's bowler-hatted henchman in the Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddjob is the mute, hat-throwing heavy who serves the villain in the 1964 James Bond picture Goldfinger.

clue.text: Radical doctor with a brief fix

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A doctor offers an extreme but quick cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe measures that are extreme and far-reaching rather than moderate.

clue.text: Creole dish Jack baked initially in a former Asian state

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word before it
in places the single letter inside the following words

blocks.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
the old name of the peninsular part of Malaysia

explanation.surface: A recipe: a dish a man named Jack first baked in an old Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside MALAYA after M, all after J and A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a spicy Louisiana rice dish with meat or seafood, a staple of Creole cooking.

clue.text: Climber has cold toffee, perhaps

blocks.note: toffee is one example of a sweet

explanation.surface: A mountaineer has a chilly piece of toffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is the woody nightshade, a scrambling plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody nightshade, a scrambling hedgerow plant with purple flowers and red berries, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Go up once more with blade, then mend one’s ways

definitions.text: Go up once more with blade

blocks.clueFragment: Go up once more with blade
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: flip a fresh blade of a plant, a blade being a leaf
second meaning: the idiom for starting to behave better

explanation.surface: Someone climbs again with a knife, and then reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: a leaf blade is turned up and over afresh. 'Blade' looks like a knife but is part of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from turning to a clean page, means abandoning bad habits and starting to behave well.

clue.text: Rodent, second seen in store

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside, so the short word sits within the shop word

blocks.note: a mart is a market or store
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A rodent is briefly spotted in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing ground squirrel of mountains and grasslands belongs to the rodent order.

clue.text: Dillinger, say, well-known by the other side and myself

blocks.note: what is well known is public
the other side in a war is the enemy
number one is slang for oneself, as in 'look after number one'

explanation.surface: Dillinger was famous even to his opponents and to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is just a joiner here: the other side gives ENEMY.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dillinger, the 1930s bank robber, was the first criminal the FBI branded with this title, the most wanted man.

clue.text: Synthetic substance: check involves smell, primarily

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the letter goes inside
primarily points at the first letter of the word before

blocks.note: to rein in is to check

explanation.surface: A lab note: test whether a man-made compound has an odour.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides tree gum, the word covers man-made polymers used in plastics, adhesives and varnishes.

clue.text: Dignified English circus clown

explanation.surface: A stately English clown performing in the circus ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The auguste is the clumsy red-nosed clown, the foil to the elegant whiteface.
explanation.definitionFit: In circus tradition this is the type of clown with baggy clothes and red nose who takes the pratfalls.

clue.text: Eccentric‘s putting game in appropriate bar

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside

blocks.note: a bar of soap is also a cake of soap

explanation.surface: An oddball is putting balls on a golf course in a suitable pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' suggests golf but means placing. FRUITCAKE is slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech a crazy or very odd person is called this, from 'nutty as a fruitcake'.

clue.text: Slam cruel, corrupt Roman general

indicators.note: corrupt letters are spoiled and changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Criticise a harsh and dishonest commander of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Claudius Marcellus was the Roman commander who captured Syracuse in the Second Punic War.

clue.text: Bishop forced out of resort town? Absolutely correct

indicators.note: forced out means removed, so that letter leaves the town name

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A cleric is driven out of a seaside town, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is the Sussex seaside resort; lose its B.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase is used as an exclamation of agreement meaning exactly right or spot on.

clue.text: Outrage about sappers being responsible for gear

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers

explanation.surface: Fury at army engineers who were in charge of the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear in the sense of clothing: this formal word means garments and attire.

clue.text: A rugby player — very large, incidentally

blocks.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: By the way, a rugby player is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word is used to introduce a remark by the way, much like 'speaking of which'.

clue.text: Utter confusion caused by half of maps produced by mapmakers

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only its first part, losing the rest

blocks.note: the Ordnance Survey, Britain's official mapmakers

explanation.surface: Total muddle arising from half the maps an agency has issued.
explanation.walkthrough: Halve CHARTS, not maps, and add the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete disorder and turmoil, the state before creation in myth, is what the word means.

clue.text: Close firm

blocks.note: first meaning: stingy, mean with money, or near
second meaning: securely fixed, not loose

explanation.walkthrough: Both look like other words: close as shut, firm as company.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something fixed securely and also a miserly or closely fitting thing.

clue.text: Couple getting book about revolutionary seed

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word is read the other way
about means surrounding, so the book word goes round

blocks.note: a tome is a big book
to seed a field is to sow it

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers acquire a book about a radical idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people, or a game played by two, is called by this word.

clue.text: Lead weapon used by chief

explanation.surface: A lead-tipped weapon wielded by a tribal chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads like the metal, but it is the verb meaning to head.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead a campaign is to lead it from the front, as the point of an attack.

clue.text: Funny turn after onset of dizziness

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, the first letter

blocks.note: to turn over is to roll

explanation.surface: A comic routine follows a dizzy spell.
explanation.definitionFit: It means amusing in a dry, wry way, a quietly humorous synonym for funny.

clue.text: Affiliated company confronting dubious agent

indicators.note: dubious suggests something not right, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A linked business faces down a shady operative.
explanation.definitionFit: Related by common origin or descent, like words from one root, is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Troublemaker in Russian government wanting new leader

indicators.note: needing a new leader means the first letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: the Moscow citadel stands for the Russian government

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker is at work inside the Russian state, which needs a fresh head.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the K of KREMLIN to G; the clue does not name the new letter, so the definition decides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for mechanical faults, and so anything causing trouble.

clue.text: Awkward situation, tho’ resolved by King Edward?

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and worked out again, so the letters rearrange

blocks.note: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato

explanation.surface: A tricky royal predicament, though one settled by the king.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch; it is a British potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate issue nobody wants to handle is called this, like a scalding vegetable passed hand to hand.

clue.text: Oxygen required by huge Greek character

explanation.surface: A giant Greek needs oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the twenty-fourth and last letter of the Greek alphabet, the character in a script.

clue.text: Declaration in part of speech, something that’s binding?

blocks.note: a word class such as he or it

explanation.surface: A formal statement within a speech carries legal force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' suggests a contract; it is a substance that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or authoritative public statement or announcement is a declaration.

clue.text: Rowing types, terrible moaners

indicators.note: terrible suggests something mangled into a different form

explanation.surface: Quarrelsome people are dreadful complainers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing' suggests arguing, but it means pulling oars.
explanation.definitionFit: People who row boats, members of a crew pulling oars, are the rowing types.

clue.text: For example, leader of group and top boffin

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An example of a group leader who is also a leading scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal, slightly mocking words for an intellectual or expert scholar.

clue.text: Opportunity taken by surgeon’s assistant: job in department store?

definitions.note: the definition names a job; the answer names the person who does it

blocks.note: a dresser assists a surgeon by dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A surgical helper seizes the chance of a job in a large shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A dresser is an old term for a surgeon's assistant who dressed wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed to arrange the displays behind the shop's front glass works this role.

clue.text: Union Party’s band?

blocks.note: surface reading: the musicians hired by a political party, or a trade union's band
setter's reading: the circle of gold worn after the union of marriage, celebrated at a party

explanation.walkthrough: Union is marriage and party is the celebration, so 'band' is a ring, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain metal band given at a marriage ceremony and worn on the finger to mark the union.

clue.text: Easily moved about male priest, the focus of attention

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the others

blocks.note: a light thing is easily moved
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A man of the cloth is easily swayed, yet everybody watches him.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, the Old Testament priest, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: The intense glare once used on stages now stands for public attention and fame.

clue.text: Novel, these swallowing bitter aloes at the start

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so a word goes within
at the start means only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A new kind of food: these folk swallow bitter aloes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new'; it is the book, Nicholas Monsarrat's 1951 war story at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Monsarrat's 1951 book about a wartime Atlantic convoy escort is a famous British work of fiction.

clue.text: Done messing with gun: prison the result

indicators.note: messing with something jumbles it up into disorder

explanation.surface: Finished playing with a firearm, he ends up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground cell in a castle where prisoners were held is this type of prison.

clue.text: Argument against reflecting on trial? That’s a foregone conclusion

indicators.note: a reflection appears back to front, so the little word is read the other way

blocks.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Objections raised during a court case, though the verdict was never in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed ON comes first, then the argument against, then the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a contest so one-sided that the outcome was never in doubt.

clue.text: Mechanical man in car on about rug

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joined words go round the floor covering

explanation.surface: A robot riding in a car sits on a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-operating machine built to look and move like a person is an automaton.

clue.text: A suture’s come loose around old outfit

indicators.note: stitches that come loose fall apart, letting the letters reform
around signals that the extra letter is mixed in with the rest

explanation.surface: A surgical stitch works loose around an elderly patient's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen gathered for her marriage is this outfit.

clue.text: Ended up expelled

blocks.note: first meaning: proved to be in the end

explanation.walkthrough: Two plain meanings, one of things resolving and one of being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both 'proved to be in the end' and 'evicted or forced out'.

clue.text: Pleasant hugging European relative

indicators.note: hugging wraps round, so one word goes outside the letter

explanation.surface: A friendly person embraces a relation from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Bone is broken by northern copper

indicators.note: a word broken by others is split open with them inserted

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A bone was fractured by a policeman from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The anvil-shaped small bone in the middle ear is this bone.

clue.text: Free from bacteria — theatre, ultimately, following new creation of Lister

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter is used
a new creation from a word remakes its letters in another order

explanation.surface: Joseph Lister's antiseptic invention made the operating theatre germ-free.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery, so the answer suits him.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely clean and free of germs and microorganisms, as surgical instruments must be.

clue.text: Intimidating woman filled with love for cavalryman

indicators.note: filled with means the letter is put inside

blocks.note: a fierce woman is a dragon
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A formidable woman is full of love for a mounted soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a mounted infantryman, and later a cavalry soldier in a regiment of that name.

clue.text: A musical work, perhaps from Bart, for musicians

definitions.note: a musical is one example of the answer

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Lionel Bart wrote a musical for performers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lionel Bart wrote the musical Oliver!, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical is one example of a creative genre or medium such as opera, ballet or poetry.

clue.text: Jogger grabbing a rest

indicators.note: grabbing something takes it inside, so the letter goes within

blocks.note: something that jogs the memory is a reminder

explanation.surface: A runner stops to take a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' suggests a runner and 'rest' a break; really a memory-jogger and what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest of something is what is left, the part that remains after the rest is taken away.

clue.text: Possible mole in border, third in garden

indicators.note: the third letter of the following word is the one kept

blocks.note: a border is a side or edge

explanation.surface: A mole lurks in the flower bed, just three plants into the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' suggests the animal in a garden border; it is a spy within.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy within an organisation, someone on the inside with privileged access.

clue.text: With vigour, teachers producing biscuit

blocks.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: Energetic teachers baking biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard, spiced round British biscuit flavoured with the root of a tropical plant.

clue.text: Defiant remark from habitual drunkard present

blocks.note: to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A boozer who is in attendance makes a cheeky retort.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a childish retort of triumph or defiance, used to end an argument.

clue.text: Name of book lieutenant raised in the course of relationship

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means written upwards, back to front
in the course of means within, so the short piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A book's name for a lieutenant brought up during an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The name by which a book, film or other work is known.

clue.text: Fur, first of bargains in market

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
in places that letter inside the next word

explanation.surface: Furs are the pick of the bargains at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark, valuable fur of a small Asian marten-like animal is known by this name.

clue.text: Praise book to a smaller extent

blocks.note: less means to a smaller extent

explanation.surface: Speak well of a book, though not too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify or extol, especially God, is one meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Peninsula in Russian region, not small

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation is taken away

blocks.note: the vast Asian part of Russia

explanation.surface: A tongue of land in Russia that is not small.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain and Portugal occupy this peninsula in south-west Europe.

clue.text: Really hard individuals over the top about morality

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the abbreviation is read the other way

blocks.note: H is hard, as on pencils
OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: Very tough people are excessive about ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really' looks like an adverb modifying 'hard'; it is the exclamation and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of sincerity meaning genuinely or truly, used to stress a claim.

clue.text: Channel close to Viking, say

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, its last letter

explanation.surface: A sea channel near the Norse raiders, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a homophone signal or 'for example'; it simply means utter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter is a channel for carrying away rainwater at a roof edge or roadside.

clue.text: Cheeky rascal, pupil throwing stone

indicators.note: throwing something away discards it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A cheeky little rascal of a pupil hurls a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone as the British weight of fourteen pounds is abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: It means rudely disrespectful and bold, just as a cheeky child is.

clue.text: Land mass area? US, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful, not right, so the letters go into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a continent might be the size of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe and Asia together form the largest continuous continental mass on Earth.
